Bauhaus table lamp (Wagenfeld and Jucker)

The “Bauhaus lamp”: an opal glass hemisphere on a straight shaft over a round base, all parts plain geometric solids.

Source
Bauhaus Kooperation: Bauhaus-Leuchte
Creator
Wilhelm Wagenfeld and Carl Jakob Jucker
Made
1923–1924 (MoMA); 1924 (Bauhaus Kooperation, credited to Wagenfeld)
Style
Bauhaus (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Rational, precise, calm
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected, in the scratchpad only, the metal version photographed by Joachim Fliegner on the Bauhaus Kooperation page and a Commons photograph by Sailko_e_di_Wilhelm_Wagenfeld_(right,_1924)_(cropped).JPG) of the glass-base version at Weimar.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Bauhaus Kooperation says Wagenfeld made the lamp in 1924, planned it as a general-purpose lamp for living rooms, and followed the geometric rules of his teacher László Moholy-Nagy. Bauhaus Kooperation.

MoMA credits Wilhelm Wagenfeld and Carl Jakob Jucker, 1923–1924. MoMA 4056.

Observed

  • A white opal glass shade is close to a hemisphere and sits on a thin flat metal ring.
  • A threaded metal collar with a pull switch joins the shade to a straight cylindrical shaft.
  • One version has a clear glass shaft and a thick clear glass disc base, with the wire visible inside the shaft.
  • The other version has a polished metal shaft and a flat metal disc base on small ball feet.
  • The pull chain ends in a small metal ball.

Why it belongs

The lamp is the object form of the style’s shape vocabulary. The glass version also shows “honest materials”: the wire and fittings stay visible.

Borrow

Combine one hemisphere, one cylinder, and one disc; do not add transitions or decoration.

Leave functional parts, such as a switch or cable, visible and neat.
